title: Strawberry and Rhubarb Iced Tea
changes_from_base: Black tea sweetened with a strained rhubarb syrup and poured over sliced strawberries; no lemon or mint.
summary: Black iced tea sweetened with a quick pink rhubarb syrup and poured over sliced strawberries, sharp and fruity rather than lemony.

steps.title: Tea
steps.text: Pour the boiling water over the tea bags in a large heatproof jug and steep for 4 minutes, then lift the bags out without pressing; squeezing them releases bitter tannins. Add the cold water, let it cool and chill for at least an hour.

steps.title: Rhubarb syrup
steps.text: While the tea cools, simmer the rhubarb with the water and sugar over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, stirring now and then, until it breaks into shreds and the liquid turns pink.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Set a sieve over a bowl, tip in the rhubarb and let the syrup drip through for 10 minutes, pressing gently. Discard the pulp, then cool and chill the syrup.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Stir the syrup into the cold tea and taste. Very tart rhubarb may want a spoonful more sugar.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Layer the strawberry slices with ice in tall glasses and pour the tea over.

tips: Pressing the rhubarb pulp hard through the sieve makes the syrup cloudy; press lightly.
Green rhubarb tastes fine but gives a paler colour; red stalks give the prettiest pink.
Add the strawberries to the glasses, not the jug, so they stay firm.
storage: Keep the tea and the syrup in the fridge for up to 3 days, apart or mixed. Slice the strawberries just before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
